We often talk about the future of energy as something we need to design. But in the Pacific, that future is already taking shape.

While global fuel prices rising above $1.50 per litre are now creating urgency, Pacific countries have long faced prices above $2, with fossil fuel imports absorbing up to 25% of GDP. What is now a shock elsewhere has been a structural reality here for decades.

That experience is shaping a different model of energy transition, not just a shift from diesel to renewables, but a transformation linking energy with transport, food systems, digital infrastructure, and resilience. Across the region, this is already visible: systems are more distributed, more data-driven, and more tightly connected to local value chains.

At UNDP , through our Rising Up for SIDS 🏝️ offer, we see energy not in isolation, but as a system that connects climate action, economic opportunity, and digital innovation into a single development pathway.

As we head into the 6th Pacific Regional Energy and Transport Ministers’ Meeting (PRETMM), this way of thinking feels increasingly relevant. 

On May 5 in Port Moresby, @UNDP Papua New Guinea co-organized a side event together with the Government of Papua New Guinea and the @Pacific Community-SPC, “From Regulation to Results: Scaling Off-Grid Energy in the Pacific,” focused on how countries are moving from policy to implementation, scaling decentralized solutions, and building investable energy systems at pace.

The opportunity now is to scale what is already working, by aligning policy, finance, technology, and delivery.

Looking forward to the discussions ahead.
